feed.title: PatchLabs changelog
feed.subtitle: What PatchLabs shipped, and when. Real entries only.

entry.title: PatchLabs v3: four product lines, and checks that read your code
entry.summary: Four product lines (Lab, Code, Fix, Watch). PatchLabs Code reads the repo on every check: secret keys in code (PL-009), open Edge Functions using the service key (PL-017), sign-ups without email confirmation (PL-018), roles in user_metadata (PL-019), browser-only admin checks (PL-020), unverified payment webhooks (PL-021), trusted user ids (PL-022), vulnerable dependencies via OSV (PL-023), raw HTML (PL-024), open Firebase rules (PL-025), risky CORS (PL-026). One finding format across report and API. Findings library PL-001 to PL-026 and Learn guides. Demo, integrations and solutions pages. Coming, not shipped: Lab checks PL-012 to PL-016; automatic pull requests with the GitHub App.

entry.title: PatchLabs v2: accounts, monitoring and proof anyone can verify
entry.summary: New website; email-link accounts and workspaces; monitoring with weekly or monthly re-checks, diffs, email alerts and Slack-compatible webhooks; badges and public status; Ed25519-signed receipts; owner decisions and answers; REST API and API keys; remote MCP server; free RLS check with no sign-up; one-click commit of the fix on GitHub; plans.

entry.title: First public leak checks
entry.summary: Public leak checks from a GitHub repo with ownership proof, reports by email and a spend cap per check. Autonomous run on 20 new apps: 18 of 20 fixes passed the strict lab proof with no human (n=20); 15 needed only the smallest model; median 3.5 minutes per app.

entry.title: Fix agents re-verified: 19 of 20 worked first time
entry.summary: We re-verified 20 real fixes written by our agents: 19 of 20 worked first time and applied cleanly (n=20, 5 Nov 2026).
